subject: Post-call: Pilot kickoff proposal — performance targets & GPU options
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@orionhealth.ai>, Sam Ortiz <s.ortiz@orionhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + pilot proposal (performance targets & GPU options)

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the primary risk areas. Quick recap from our side and a proposed pilot design so we can validate the SLOs you need before a Dedicated reservation.

TL;DR — what we heard from Orion Health:
- p95 latency target: <= 200 ms for interactive endpoint (model: LLM-derivative, gen up to ~512 tokens typical)
- Sustained throughput: ~120 QPS across two routes (inference + re-rank), peak bursts to ~220 QPS for 2-3 minutes
- Concurrency: up to 48 concurrent sessions (user-facing streaming) with stable P95 requirements
- Streaming: server-side token streaming required (partial tokens shown to UI within 100–150ms of generation)

Proposed pilot (attached: pilot-spec-v1.pdf + gpu-comparison-matrix.csv):
- Duration: 2-week controlled pilot in our Dedicated staging pool
- Config A (performance-first): 2x H100-80GB, NVLink, 1 node reserved for steady-state + burst pool (aim: single-model p95 headroom)
- Config B (cost-balanced): 4x A10G or A100-40GB equivalence split across 2 nodes (aim: similar throughput via sharding; lower per-hour cost)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end streaming latency (first token latency), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, per-token cost (estimated)
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 200ms for common prompt mix, no more than 2% request errors at peak, consistent streaming first-token latency <= 150ms

Open questions for you (please confirm in reply):
1) Typical prompt+response token distribution (we estimated 30% short <64, 60% medium 64–512, 10% long >512).
2) Any hard constraints on cold-starts / absolute single-request latency SLAs for critical workflows?
3) Will you be able to run synthetic load tests from your infra, or should Redwood generate representative traffic?

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm the token distribution + accept pilot plan (we’ll send a DocuSign quote for the Reserved pilot).
- Kickoff call to align on data/keys and a short test harness (30–45 mins).
- Pilot start (2 weeks) with mid-pilot check at day 7.

Attaching initial quote and perf matrix for visibility. Ben will follow-up on the kernel/runtime tuning knobs we’ll exercise during the pilot.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pilot proposal (performance targets & GPU options)

Thanks, Evelyn — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token distribution: your estimate is close. We ran a sampling job last quarter and saw ~35% short (<64), 55% medium (64–512), 10% long (>512). Peak burst pattern: sustained for ~120–180s then drops.
- Streaming behavior: UI needs first token within 120–150ms in 95% of cases; after that streaming throughput is tolerant to small jitter.
- Cold-starts: we cannot tolerate more than 400ms cold-start p95 for critical flows (we prefer warm pools).

On GPUs: cost will be a factor for us — we’d like Redwood’s recommendation on H100 vs A100 vs A10G given (a) our p95 latency goals, (b) constrained budget for the pilot (we can commit to a 2-week paid pilot but would prefer a cost-efficient baseline).

We can generate synthetic traffic for the test harness; Sam (cc) will share the load profile. Please send over any requirements for keys/whitelist IPs.

—Dana

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pilot proposal (performance targets & GPU options)

Thanks Dana — appreciate the token distribution and the cold-start constraint. A few concrete engineering notes and a recommended test matrix so we can size Dedicated correctly.

Quick answers: H100 vs A100 vs A10G tradeoffs (short summary):
- H100 (FP16/FP8) — best single-card throughput for large-context, mixed-precision models; lower latency per token when kernel fusion + NVLink used; higher hourly cost but fewer nodes required for same QPS. Good if you need tight p95 headroom and want smaller cluster footprint.
- A100 (40/80GB) — strong middle ground; predictable performance for transformer workloads; cheaper than H100 in some regions; will need 1.5–2x more cards than H100 for the same peak QPS in our benchmarks for 512-token flows.
- A10G / L40-ish class — cost-effective for shardable workloads and where you can scale horizontally; higher inter-node networking impact on streaming first-token latency unless we pin a model per GPU and keep requests local.

Suggested pilot test matrix (we’ll run each scenario for 3–4 hours of ramped steady-state + bursts):
- Test 1 (latency-focused): 2x H100, single-model, warm KV cache, streaming enabled. Measure first-token latency and p95 across prompt mixes.
- Test 2 (cost-balanced): 3x A100-40GB, sharded across 2 nodes, autoscaling off for controlled baseline. Measure p95 and per-token cost.
- Test 3 (horizontal): 5x A10G, model per GPU, synthetic ingress distributed across nodes (validate end-to-end first-token streaming latency).

Reserved throughput sizing guidance (initial):
- Baseline reserved throughput: 120 QPS sustained
- Burst pool: additional 120 QPS available (auto-burst up to 240 QPS for up to 3 minutes)
- Concurrency config: target 48 concurrent streaming sessions — we’ll size session slots per GPU based on avg tokens/sec in your sample traces

Instrumentation & gating: we’ll stream metrics to your Splunk/Datadog endpoint and also provide trace hooks in Redwood Console so you can verify end-to-end latency. Acceptance gating: if p95 > 200ms in Test 1 or first-token p95 > 150ms we’ll expand node count or fallback to H100 variant.

Ask for Sam/Infra: we need an IP allowlist range and a service account key for the pilot. Attachments: I’ve attached the GPU matrix with our observed tokens/sec across models (gpu-comparison-matrix.csv).

If this looks good I’ll catalog expected hours so finance can prep the reserved-throughput-quote.pdf (Evelyn — can you push DocuSign once the pilot config is agreed?).

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
